steps.text: To make the sauce: Bring orange juice, lemon juice, brown sugar, orange zest, and lemon zest to a boil in a saucepan over medium-high heat. Reduce heat to medium-low and simmer until slightly thickened, about 5 minutes.
Remove from heat and stir in vanilla extract. Set aside to cool.

Layer fruit in a large, clear glass bowl in this order: pineapple, strawberries, kiwi fruit, bananas, oranges, grapes, and blueberries. Pour cooled sauce over fruit; cover and refrigerate for 3 to 4 hours before serving.

raw_recipe.headline: Perfect Summer Fruit Salad
raw_recipe.description: This fantastic fruit salad combines pineapple, kiwi, bananas, oranges, grapes, and berries in a sweet citrusy sauce for a colorful summer dessert.

video.description: This eclectic mix of fruit will sweeten up your BBQ or any time you're craving a sweet little side dish. For this delicious fruit salad, the secret is in the sauce!

review.reviewBody: Normally I don’t care for “formal” fruit salads as they tend to include a lot of other stuff beyond the fruit – like cream, yogurt, marshmallows, nuts, etc. I appreciated the simplicity of this one which allowed the fruit itself to shine. The citrus syrup seemed to bring all the flavors together, contributed a just right sweetness and prevented the fruit from turning color. Versatile too, since this would work with whatever fruits you choose or have on hand. I made this for just Hubs and me, so I just tossed the fruit and syrup altogether and served the salad in individual dessert dishes.

I made this yesterday and it was the talk of the party. EVERYONE loved it. I did not change a thing. One change - I did not layer it but mixed it all together and it was so beautiful, mixed together. The syrup was great too. There were about 70 people at the Picnic and people kept coming back for more. I made it bigger than called for and it still went faster than anything else. A definite keeper!!! Wish I could give it more stars. I acutally cut up everything the night before except the banana, and even made the sauce the night before too. Then a few hous before I served it I tossed it together, then cut and added the banana. YUMMY

I made this for a baptism luncheon and it was all gone. This is a beautiful presentation and delicious fruit salad! I was worried about making the dish the night before as I was concerned the fruit would brown or get mushy. Instead, I made the sauce the night before(delicious) and let simmer longer than the prescribed time to thicken up and refrigerated. While simmering, I cut up all of the fruit (except for the bananas) and put in individual baggies. Instead of oranges, I used cuties. It thought they looked pretty and we love those little oranges. In the morning, I cut up the bananas and layered everything just as shown in a truffle bowl, drizzled the sauce on top, and covered with saran wrap. Perfect! I will definitely make this again. Thank you for the recipe!

Besides the unnecessarily sweet, brown sugar syrup concoction ... I see one more big improvement this recipe could benefit from.
I always used to use lemon in my fruit salads and never realized how unpleasantly sour it made the otherwise naturally sweet fruit taste. I knew it needed an acid to prevent the fruit from going bad prematurely, but it wasn't until my discovery of the distinctly Latin American influence of using limes almost to the exclusion of our invariable use of lemon for every single purpose (don't get me wrong, I LOVE lemon flavor when used appropriately like in lemon meringue pie, lemon curd, lemon cake/cookies/bars, etc etc.).
But for this recipe the only citrus fruit ever needed to add a distinctively refreshing acidity, w/o the accompanying "sour", are LIMES! No orange juice, and definitely NO LEMONS!
So go ahead and try it; put down the inevitable lemon, and squeeze a couple of limes with just a touch of plain old granulated sugar and i guarantee you not one of you reading this review will EVER go back to lemons in your fruit salad again. And your guest will surely notice the subtle "je ne sais quois" fl;avor you imparted to those deliciously ripe and sweet summer fruit you'v epicked up from your local market.
I made this for a 4th of July party and won Top Chef! 2 things I did different. I let it sit in the juices overnight and when I got to the party I scooped the fruit into waffle cones

Quadrupled the recipe to feed a large group. Yes, 4 times the amounts listed. Cannot believe the responses from guests. All but a small amount in the bottom of the bowl was left. I have since made it again just for the family. I actually doubled the amount of dressing. Worked out perfectly because we spooned the fruit mixture over dessert cakes and added whipped cream. Yum!

I've made this many times, exactly as written. Delicious, and loved by all! I made a version for a work luncheon, replacing the grapes with diced apples, as a co-worker hates grapes. I think I like that even better. Also, the left-over dressing at the bottom of the bowl is GREAT with vodka. Just sayin'.

Just change the order, strawberry, orange/tangerine, banana, pineapple, green grapes, kiwi, blueberries, purple grapes. You get a rainbow dish that displays amazingly well and wows guests until people start digging in. It also provides basically every vitamin that your body needs and compliments savoury dishes like ribs or burgers very well at a BBQ. I like to top it with vanilla flavoured Greek yogurt instead of making a sauce because that ensures it provides everything the body needs and the probiotics help you get the most nutrients out of the main course. In theory, eating just that is a balanced diet minus carbs and sodium so it’s great for health group meetings too.

I used the juice from the Pineapple, (Non-Heavy Syrup) 4 Tbsp. Local Honey, 2 Tbsp. Lime. Mixed without cooking. Mixed it in with the fruit and refrigerated it. Taking it out from time to time to fold the juices from the bottom and further mix the flavors together.

This is delicious!!! I wasn't sure if I was going to like the syrup, but was pleasantly surprised. I'm going to make again for a family BBQ this weekend. 
I just used the fruit I had on hand and it was very good. Pineapple, mango, clementines, grapes, blueberries, apple and banana. 
I think the kiwi and strawberry would go beautifully with this sauce and fresh summer peaches. I can't wait to make this again!

I used 4 kiwi, 4 bananas, 1 pound of strawberries, not so many grapes (the bowl was almost full), and 11 ounces blueberries. I increased orange juice to1 cup, 1/8 cup more lemon juice, but kept the vanilla to 1teaspoon. Next time I will will mix up the fruit instead of layering. Good recipe
It's a crowd pleaser- simple but looks beautiful
Everyone loves it!

Oops! My mistake! 😊 I forgot to turn my printed recipe page over and accidentally mixed the Citrus Sauce ingredients with the fruit before realizing the sauce was supposed to be boiled first. Even so, the fruit salad tasted delicious—it just wasn't as pretty as the photo! Tip: I stirred the sliced bananas into the Citrus Sauce before pouring it over the fruit. The citrus coated the bananas nicely and helped keep them from browning.

She is a beauty and the citrus glaze is a delight! Fun, beautiful display of color, and easy!
